features.description: ShopBot is an LLM backed chat assistant embedded in a webshop. It answers questions about order status, return policy, and product details, and escalates to a human agent on request or when unsure. It interacts directly with natural persons and generates text, but does not make decisions about people, does not profile, score, or categorize individuals, and performs no biometric processing or emotion inference.
purposes: answer customer questions about orders, returns, and products
escalate to a human support agent on request or when unsure

answer.provisional_note: These requirements are provisional pending the human-review determination of the classification. The risk category is tentative and could change, for example to Unacceptable risk, which yields zero requirements.

conditions: to AI systems authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences
subject to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of third parties
exceptions: unless those systems are available for the public to report a criminal offence

article-50.actor: providers of ai systems, including general-purpose ai systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content
conditions: generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content
exceptions: this obligation shall not apply to the extent the ai systems perform an assistive function for standard editing
this obligation shall not apply to the extent [the ai systems] do not substantially alter the input data provided by the deployer or the semantics thereof
this obligation shall not apply ... where authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences
article-50.object: that the outputs of the ai system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated

conditions: as far as this is technically feasible
taking into account the specificities and limitations of various types of content
taking into account the costs of implementation
taking into account the generally acknowledged state of the art, as may be reflected in relevant technical standards
exceptions: this obligation shall not apply to the extent the ai systems perform an assistive function for standard editing
this obligation shall not apply to the extent [the ai systems] do not substantially alter the input data provided by the deployer or the semantics thereof
this obligation shall not apply ... where authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences
article-50.object: their technical solutions are effective, interoperable, robust and reliable

article-50.actor: deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system
exceptions: this obligation shall not apply to ai systems used for biometric categorisation and emotion recognition, which are permitted by law to detect, prevent or investigate criminal offences, subject to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of third parties, and in accordance with union law
article-50.object: the natural persons exposed thereto of the operation of the system

article-50.actor: deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system
exceptions: this obligation shall not apply to ai systems used for biometric categorisation and emotion recognition, which are permitted by law to detect, prevent or investigate criminal offences, subject to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of third parties, and in accordance with union law
article-50.object: the personal data in accordance with Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and (EU) 2018/1725 and Directive (EU) 2016/680, as applicable

conditions: to ai systems used for biometric categorisation and emotion recognition
which are permitted by law to detect, prevent or investigate criminal offences
subject to appropriate safeguards for the rights and freedoms of third parties
in accordance with union law

article-50.action: limit the transparency obligations set out in this paragraph to disclosure
conditions: where the content forms part of an evidently artistic, creative, satirical, fictional or analogous work or programme
article-50.object: the existence of such generated or manipulated content in an appropriate manner that does not hamper the display or enjoyment of the work

article-50.actor: deployers of an ai system that generates or manipulates text which is published with the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest
exceptions: this obligation shall not apply where the use is authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences

this obligation shall not apply where the ai-generated content has undergone a process of human review or editorial control and where a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility for the publication of the content
article-50.object: that the text has been artificially generated or manipulated

conditions: to the natural persons concerned
in a clear and distinguishable manner
at the latest at the time of the first interaction or exposure
article-50.object: the information referred to in paragraphs 1 to 4

conditions: the information

article-50.action: encourage and facilitate the drawing up
conditions: to facilitate the effective implementation of the obligations regarding the detection and labelling of artificially generated or manipulated content
article-50.object: codes of practice at union level

conditions: in accordance with the procedure laid down in article 56 (6)
article-50.object: implementing acts to approve those codes of practice

conditions: if it deems the code is not adequate
in accordance with the examination procedure laid down in article 98(2)
article-50.object: common rules for the implementation of those obligations
